stem: A language-learning app asked its users to volunteer for a study, and 150 users volunteered. The app randomly assigned 75 of the volunteers to use a new review feature and the other 75 to use the app without it. After eight weeks, the volunteers who used the new feature had a higher average score on a vocabulary test. Which of the following statements is (are) supported by the study? I. Using the new feature likely causes higher vocabulary scores for all of the app's users. II. Using the new feature likely caused higher vocabulary scores for the volunteers in the study. III. Every volunteer who used the new feature scored higher than he or she would have scored without it.
solution: The feature was randomly assigned, so a causal conclusion is supported for the participants (II).
The participants were volunteers, not a random sample of all users, so the conclusion cannot be generalized to all users (I is not supported).
A causal effect on the average does not mean every individual benefited (III is not supported).

explanation.A: Incorrect. Statement I generalizes beyond the volunteers, which needs a random sample of all users.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Volunteers are not a random sample of all users, so statement I is not supported, while statement II is.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Statement III claims an effect for every individual; the study shows only a difference in the average.
explanation.D: Correct. Only the causal conclusion about the volunteers in the study (II) is supported.
